tasks.title: Refuse to start a worker that cannot enforce: execution-enforcement gate at boot

executionPolicy.rationale: A worker outside its delegated cgroup executes every task with rlimit-only enforcement while the record still looks complete; refusing at boot is the only way the absence stays visible.

acceptanceCriteria: A worker started outside the delegated subtree exits non-zero before opening a Temporal connection.
The refusal names the actual cgroup, the expected cgroup path and every failing check.
A correctly launched worker (infra/scripts/worker-with-cgroup.sh) verifies and polls.
The opt-out exists, is configurable, defaults to off, and is documented as control-plane only.

evidenceRequirement.note: 29 tests: parsing, path-segment containment, controller and limit refusals, the source-order assertion that the gate precedes NativeConnection.connect, and the real-host verdict.

tasks.title: Dispose test-owned cgroup leaves on every path and reconcile the leftovers

executionPolicy.rationale: A leaked leaf keeps charging the delegation root and can hold a live process; cleanup that returns a boolean nobody reads is not a cleanup path.

acceptanceCriteria: A leaf is killed, verified empty and removed on success, assertion failure, timeout and forced child termination.
rmdir is never attempted while cgroup.procs is non-empty.
Reconciliation deletes only names the test suites produce; the launcher leaf and workspace-id leaves are refused.
The three leaves recorded in IO-ENFORCEMENT-PROOF.md section 8 are each measured and resolved or refused.

evidenceRequirement.note: 16 tests, including the refusal to rmdir a non-empty leaf, the refusal when cgroup.procs cannot be read, and the name allowlist that excludes worker and UUID leaves.

tasks.title: Remove passwordless sudo from the uid that runs the worker

executionPolicy.rationale: This is a sudoers change on a live host; no code gate can carry it and the change requires operator authorisation before it is applied.

acceptanceCriteria: sudo -n true exits non-zero for the worker uid.
Password sudo still works for the four bootstrap scripts, proven in a new session.
A sudoers backup exists and its restore path is written down before the change.

evidenceRequirement.note: Steps 1 and 2 of the remediation sequence; needs authorisation per section 7.

tasks.title: Split broker and sandbox identities so peer credentials discriminate

executionPolicy.rationale: The broker socket currently accepts the worker and the sandbox as the same peer, so SO_PEERCRED cannot distinguish the two and an authorisation check on it would be theatre.

acceptanceCriteria: izbroker and izsandbox exist as separate nologin identities.
The broker socket is 0660 izbroker:izsandbox and the peer uid is checked on connect.
The worker uid cannot read the credential store by path.

evidenceRequirement.note: A broker test that asserts a connect from each uid, with the worker refused.

tasks.title: Execute the authored CI workflow against a real Temporal service

executionPolicy.rationale: The workflow is authored and has never run; a pipeline that has never executed is a configuration file, not a gate.

acceptanceCriteria: The workflow runs to completion once on a push or a manual dispatch.
The run proves the Temporal-dependent suites execute rather than skip.
The skip budget reporter is visible in the job log.

evidenceRequirement.note: Needs a git remote and a push credential; see PHASE7-GATE-MATRIX.md R-17.

tasks.title: Prove a backup restores by performing an isolated restore drill

executionPolicy.rationale: A backup that has never been restored is not a recovery process, and the drill needs a destination this host does not have.

acceptanceCriteria: A backup is taken, restored into an isolated database, and queried for a known tenant row.
The restore duration and the recovery point are recorded.
The drill is repeatable from a documented script.

evidenceRequirement.note: Gate recorded BLOCKED; needs a destination and an authorisation.

tasks.title: Apply io.max inside per-attempt leaves, not only the worker leaf

executionPolicy.rationale: The I/O proof measured the worker leaf; agent workloads run in per-attempt leaves, where io.max has never been applied and would otherwise be assumed from the parent's numbers.

acceptanceCriteria: An attempt leaf carries io.max for the configured device before the process starts.
A write beyond the limit is throttled inside the attempt leaf and recorded.
Read bandwidth and iops dimensions are measured or explicitly excluded.

evidenceRequirement.note: Extends the existing suite; section 7 of IO-ENFORCEMENT-PROOF.md lists this as not established.

tasks.title: Prove per-attempt accounting under two concurrent attempts

executionPolicy.rationale: Every measurement so far is a single attempt; cross-attempt accounting in one parent cgroup is unmeasured and would show up as a wrong cpu_time_ms on a real attempt.

acceptanceCriteria: Two attempts run simultaneously in separate leaves and each records only its own usage.
Neither attempt's kill affects the other's process tree.
The parent's subtree-wide counters are reconciled against the two children.

evidenceRequirement.note: Section 5 item 1 of CPU-MEMORY-ENFORCEMENT-PROOF.md records this as unproven.

tasks.title: Decide and enforce a swap policy for agent workloads

executionPolicy.rationale: Swap is fully consumed on this host, there is no per-workload swap policy, and a memory limit interacting with an exhausted swap device is untested.

acceptanceCriteria: The policy is stated: swap allowed, bounded, or denied for agent workloads.
memory.swap.max is set per attempt and read back, or its absence is recorded.
An attempt under memory pressure is classified the same way twice.

evidenceRequirement.note: Section 5 records swap at 100 percent of 4 GiB.

tasks.title: Independent review of the Phase 7 and Phase 8 SHA

executionPolicy.rationale: Gate G had seven independent rounds and Phase 7 had none; the gate this phase added is itself unreviewed by anyone but its author.

acceptanceCriteria: A reviewer who did not write the gate reads apps/worker/src/execution-enforcement.ts and its tests.
Every claim in the Phase 8 documents is checked against the repository, not the transcript.
Findings are recorded with severity and disposition.

evidenceRequirement.note: The Phase 6 review is the template; R-20 is PARTIAL for Phase 7 and Phase 8.

tasks.title: Write the two Phase 7 documents the matrix claims

executionPolicy.rationale: R-21 cites GATE-M-SUMMARY.md and EVIDENCE-INDEX-PHASE7.md; neither exists, which is the documentation defect class the claim audit exists for.

acceptanceCriteria: Both files exist under docs/engineering/phase7-host-boundary/ and are cited from R-21.
Every file reference in the Phase 7 and Phase 8 documents resolves on disk.
R-21 moves from PARTIAL only when the filesystem agrees.

evidenceRequirement.note: R-21 was corrected to PARTIAL in Phase 8 rather than deleted, so the gap stays visible.

tasks.title: Prove io.max throttles a real process on the delegated worker leaf

executionPolicy.rationale: A resource claim is only a control if a real process is measurably slowed; a configured io.max nobody measured proves nothing.

acceptanceCriteria: Unconstrained and constrained writes measured on the same block device
The constrained process confirmed inside 0::/intelligenz/worker
io.max restored to max and the scratch files removed

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 1cf3c58. 245 MB/s unconstrained vs 4.3 MB/s at wbps=4194304, a 57x reduction matching the configured 4 MiB/s, process in 0::/intelligenz/worker, io.stat attribution on 259:0.

tasks.title: Parent programme workflow dispatching child task workflows, with a three-task continuation proof

executionPolicy.rationale: The parent refuses to dispatch an invalid graph and never authorises execution; a programme that can dispatch around the claim or the approval gate reopens the O1 defect.

acceptanceCriteria: One submission and no further calls: three dependent tasks reach succeeded
Checkpoints recorded in dependency order, each naming the claim of its own attempt
A permanently failed node blocks only its dependents while independent branches still succeed

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 2321c0d. Rows read back: Programme succeeded, 3 checkpoints in order, 3 tasks each with its own claimed attempt. Isolation: B failed, C blocked at the scheduler with attemptCount 0, D succeeded.

tasks.title: Stop the gRPC retry timer outliving the channel so e2e exits 0

executionPolicy.rationale: A suite that reports 141 passed and exits 1 is a false red, and a false red trains everyone to ignore the exit code.

acceptanceCriteria: Offline suites schedule no gRPC retry timer at all
e2e reports the same counts and exits 0 repeatedly
No unhandledRejection handler or ignore-errors flag introduced

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit b4408e8. maxAttempts 10 gave an uncaught Channel error 3/3; maxAttempts 1 gave clean exit 3/3, and e2e fell from 75.8s to 24-40s because the retry chain no longer exists.

executionPolicy.rationale: The new ability to mint an ExecutionAttempt from the scheduler was unreviewed; a boundary nobody challenged is a boundary nobody knows.

acceptanceCriteria: HEAD, branch, worktree and the 18 models / 9 migrations / 10 activities are verified from the filesystem, not the report.
An independent reviewer answers ten authority questions with file:line citations.
The lead re-verifies every load-bearing claim before accepting it; disagreements are recorded, not smoothed.
Authority verdicts are recorded per boundary as ENFORCED / PARTIAL / UNENFORCED, never as a single overall PASS.

evidenceRequirement.note: Review delivered 11 findings. Six load-bearing facts re-verified by the lead, including the SDK child-id default, the cancel target, the checkpoint upsert predicate and the reservation check order.

tasks.title: Reconcile the 8.6 baseline and commission an independent authority review

executionPolicy.rationale: Two HIGH defects made a lost activity response wedge a task, and made a cancelled task report success. Both were reachable without any attacker.

acceptanceCriteria: A retried reservation that finds its own committed rows answers `reserved`, not `not_runnable`.
A programme child runs under `task-<taskId>`, so cancellation reaches it and the checkpoint names an execution an operator can re-probe.
A cancel that Temporal answers `not_found` refuses with 409 and writes nothing locally.
A reservation whose child never starts is compensated: run and attempt failed, task back to `ready` under a CAS.
A terminal programme refuses a reservation, and `load` reports the status it committed.
A task held elsewhere is recorded `blocked`, not `failed`; a genuinely failed task stays `failed`.
A checkpoint sequence collision cannot relabel another task row.
The PROGRAMME_AUTHORITY_REFUSED arm has a test that fails if the equality check is removed.

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 34eaedf. 11 tests (3 pre-existing + 8 new), each named after the defect. Lead re-ran: 11/11. Full suite 1024 passed / 15 skipped; API e2e 142; typecheck 0; lint 0.

tasks.title: Close the seven programme authority defects the review found

executionPolicy.rationale: A proposal is untrusted data. If validation is part of the planner, the planner can pass itself.

acceptanceCriteria: A strict, versioned proposal schema; unknown fields are refused so provenance cannot be smuggled in.
Graph rules are delegated to `validateProgrammeGraph`; no second cycle detector exists.
Title and goal caps match `CreateTaskInput`, so a plan that validates can actually be materialised.
A schema-valid but unschedulable proposal is reported with structured issues, never silently repaired.
The canonical content hash is stable under task reordering and changes when one criterion changes.

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit fced403. 24 contract tests plus 9 existing graph tests, re-run by the lead. `node:crypto` lives in a separate non-barrel subpath because contracts is bundled into the Temporal sandbox.

tasks.title: Define the proposal contract and reuse the one graph validator

executionPolicy.rationale: Plan approval must never become execution authority. The test is row counts: approve writes none.

acceptanceCriteria: Approval creates zero Task, zero Programme and zero ExecutionAttempt rows, asserted by counts before and after.
The approver is the JWT subject; no body field can name an approver, a status or a hash.
Four-eyes is enforced through the existing `allowsSelfApproval` policy and audited on refusal.
Submission refuses a changed proposal (hash), an expired approval, and a proposal that no longer validates.
Duplicate submission yields one programme; duplicate proposal with the same Idempotency-Key calls the model once.
The planner’s risk class is a claim; the server derives the effective class and never spends a grant.
An unconfigured provider answers 503 and writes no row.

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 0a222ba. 17 e2e tests against a 127.0.0.1 stub with no internet. Lead re-ran the suite: 159 passed. Provider is `http-llm` only; there is no heuristic fallback planner.

tasks.title: Persist plans and separate the approval decision from submission

executionPolicy.rationale: Prose that embeds task ids cannot be filtered or charted; "blocked because an approval is pending" and "blocked because a dependency failed" were only distinguishable by parsing English.

acceptanceCriteria: A closed code vocabulary; NULL means the row predates the column and is read as UNSPECIFIED, never as success.
The code is written in the same conditional UPDATE as the terminal status, and cleared on success.
The code rides the `programme.finished.v1` audit payload so telemetry can read it without a second write.
A succeeded programme returns null, not UNSPECIFIED.

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 0b68b9b. Includes an exact-ten-codes drift guard; worker tests assert APPROVAL_PENDING, TASK_FAILED and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on real programmes.

tasks.title: Give a programme stop reason a machine-readable code

executionPolicy.rationale: The mechanism existed and had never been crossed. A boundary asserted to exist is not a boundary proved to work.

acceptanceCriteria: A real workflow crosses the boundary at least twice and finishes succeeded.
The checkpoint sequence is carried forward, not restarted at zero.
Every checkpoint names the attempt that claimed it, across the boundary.
A negative control with the boundary above the checkpoint count does not cross, so the positive assertion is not always true.
The crossing is established from the execution history, not from a code path or a log line.

evidenceRequirement.note: Commit 0b68b9b. 3 runs, 2 crossings, history link read from `WorkflowExecutionContinuedAsNew` (describe() does not expose it in SDK 1.25.0). The test forced a real fix: the backstop compared the cumulative sequence, which would have continued for ever after the first crossing.

tasks.title: Prove the Continue-As-New boundary by crossing it

executionPolicy.rationale: PostHog has never ingested an event from this project. A dashboard built now would be a drawing, and a property carrying an objective would ship user content to a third party.

acceptanceCriteria: Twelve events mapped to the transition that triggers them, each marked existing or proposed.
Every property is an enum, count, internal id or bucketed duration; no prompts, goals, criteria, paths, notes or hashes.
Deduplication is the audit idempotency key as `$insert_id`; the audit log is the source of truth.
Product and operational classes are separated so blocked work cannot inflate adoption.

evidenceRequirement.note: Design only. No projector exists and no event was sent. States plainly that ingested_event=false means no adoption claim is possible.

tasks.title: Define the telemetry event contract without emitting anything

executionPolicy.rationale: The most likely user error is reading a clean proposed plan as an authorised one.

acceptanceCriteria: Every plan and programme status has a label, a tone and an explicit "never" list.
Approve is disabled for a non-admin, a proposer, an invalid plan, and its reason is shown rather than hidden.
Approval and submission are never one gesture.
A blocked programme shows its reason code and states that approving the task does not resume the programme.
Status is conveyed by text plus colour; the dependency table is the accessible representation.

evidenceRequirement.note: Requirements only. No Figma file key was supplied, no file was created, no credits spent, no UI code changed.

tasks.title: Specify the control-plane UX without building it

executionPolicy.rationale: Whether a stopped programme may be re-opened is a scheduling-authority decision, not inferable from the approval policy. Implementing it without the decision would invent governance.

acceptanceCriteria: A policy decision records who may re-open a blocked programme and whether that is the same row.
Whether an approval decision may cause a dispatch attempt is decided, not assumed.
Resume count and deadline behaviour are decided.
Any implementation re-enters through the reservation authority check and never spends a grant.
Duplicate resume and duplicate approval cannot produce two executions.

evidenceRequirement.note: BLOCKED. Three independent blockers verified: the workflow closed under ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY, nothing observes a decision, and the terminal row is refused by the reservation. D1-D3 are blocking; no endpoint or schema field was added.

tasks.title: Resume an approval-gated programme node after a valid decision

executionPolicy.rationale: Cancellation of a programme is reachable only out of band today; the workflow half works but no API route names programme-<id>, so journey 8 is partial.

acceptanceCriteria: POST /programmes/:id/cancel reaches programme-<id> and does not write the terminal status locally.
The non-cancellable scope records `cancelled` with code CANCELLED and no further node is dispatched.
A not_found answer refuses rather than writing a local cancellation.
A test asserts the durable terminal row and that no task started after it.

evidenceRequirement.note: NOT DONE. Deferred deliberately rather than added unverified at the end of a session. The child-cancellation half is proven by commit 34eaedf.

tasks.title: Add a programme cancellation endpoint that stops dispatch

executionPolicy.rationale: One failure in eight full-suite runs, then seven consecutive passes and a clean isolated run. Calling it flaky without the assertion would be a guess; calling it fixed would be a lie.

acceptanceCriteria: The failing assertion is captured from a real failing run.
The mechanism is identified as product (a status code under contention) or harness (interleaving).
If product, the specific defect is fixed and a regression test fails without the fix.
If harness, the test asserts the same property without depending on scheduling.

evidenceRequirement.note: NOT REPRODUCED after ~95 executions: 8 then 7 full-suite runs, 40 consecutive isolated runs of the spec, 50 batches of an n-way reproducer at 2 and 4 contenders. The lock-cycle hypothesis was disproven by measurement (FOR NO KEY UPDATE is compatible with FOR KEY SHARE). The test now attaches statuses, codes and row counts to its failure message; assertions and expected values are unchanged. Blocked on a captured occurrence, not on an unknown cause.

tasks.title: Reproduce the intermittent approval-attempt-binding e2e failure

executionPolicy.rationale: On the deadline path the row says timed_out while the returned result derives blocked from node states. A return value that contradicts the durable row is the class of inconsistency this programme exists to remove.

acceptanceCriteria: The deadline path returns status timed_out, matching the row.
No other terminal path returns a status the row does not hold.
A test asserts the return value and the row together.

evidenceRequirement.note: OPEN, disclosed by P87-006. Pre-existing; deliberately not fixed at the end of the session without its own verification.

tasks.title: Make the workflow return value agree with the terminal row on the deadline path

history.summary: Phase 8 baseline: the Phase 7 matrix was reconciled against the filesystem, two cited documents were confirmed absent, and R-21 was corrected to PARTIAL rather than deleted.

R-11 measured at the full tier through the documented launcher: 16 passed, 0 skipped, the three cgroup kill tests executed. The remaining boundary was that nothing refused a worker started outside the leaf.
R-13 measured on block device 259:0: write bandwidth enforced on a real process and read back from io.max. Per-attempt enforcement and read bandwidth recorded as not established.

The boot gate landed: a worker outside the delegated subtree now exits non-zero before opening a Temporal connection, and a correctly launched one verifies. Leaf hygiene added; oom-684210-31881 was empty and removed, cpu-budget-857041-28855 holds a live process and was refused, oom3-687854 matches no test naming pattern and was refused.

Programme layer built and proven: one submission drives three dependent tasks with no further calls, and a failed node blocks only its dependents. I/O write throttling proven on the worker leaf; the gRPC teardown false red removed at its source.

Phase 8.7: the programme authority boundary was independently reviewed and seven defects were closed; a proposal-only planner was added with plan approval kept separate from submission and from per-task approval; a programme stop reason became machine-readable; the Continue-As-New boundary was crossed in a real test, which exposed a would-be infinite continuation loop and forced its fix. Approval resumption is blocked on governance decisions D1-D3 and was not invented.

P87-011 investigated and not reproduced: ~95 executions clean, including 40 consecutive runs of the failing spec and 50 n-way contention batches. The plausible deadlock was disproven with a direct lock-order probe rather than assumed. The test now captures the evidence a future failure needs, with no assertion changed. The task stays blocked; it is not declared fixed.
